event.summary: Removed output reaping barriers do not leave a replacement control client overlapping
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing the output-reap and session-sink barriers could let disconnect or takeover crash the shared terminal server and lose running sessions. Suggested bucket: highest if the old tmux-control-client route remained; could-be-highest: true. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for this assigned removal, not runtime observation. Source/contract: the replacement ActiveAttach at terminals.rs:431-458 holds HostAttach and an in-process GridSender task, with join_forwarder at 478-483. service/grid_stream.rs:937-965 selects shutdown against the whole stream, drops that stream before synchronous report_forwarder_end, and owns no control-mode child. HostAttach::drop at grid_stream.rs:1169-1175 signals cancellation; Pump::run at 1201-1241 selects that cancellation both while waiting and handing input over. service/teardown.rs:1237-1255 signals all drained tasks before joining any. SPEC_impl.md:1963-1981 says every terminal served is a terminal host; each host runtime independently owns its connection (2098-2128), unlike an attachment's removed tmux client. proposed_drop: refuted by replacement ownership and cancellation code; removing the tmux process reaping barrier cannot produce its former output-client overlap hazard because the replacement holds no such process. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: this resolves only the removed output-client lifecycle mechanism, not every terminal-host input/order behavior or the separately specified startup retirement policy.

event.summary: Atomic stop flag retains the locked attach-admission boundary
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether replacing the sink registry's stopping flag with an atomic lets a new terminal attachment install after orderly shutdown drains the existing ones. Suggested bucket: high if established; could-be-highest: false (this check concerns a stranded attachment, with no source route to lost processes or user data). Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no runtime observation. Source: service/teardown.rs:1237-1255 acquires attachments and stores attachments_closed=true before draining it. service/handlers.rs:1740-1754 checks is_stopping under that same attachments lock before creating output tasks or installing an attachment. terminals.rs:490-493 reads the flag with SeqCst. Thus the atomic does not replace the lock that serializes installation against the drain; it only stores the closed state. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams (2626-2676) preserves shared attachment machinery while terminals remain independently driven. proposed_drop: refuted by the common attachments lock in the writer and reader. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: shutdown_output_clients may time out while waiting for that lock, as its documented budget allows; that is separate from an atomic visibility or check/install race.

event.summary: Removing the pane-death latch does not discard the host terminal's final screen
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing AttachBackend::observed_death and PaneDeath makes an exited agent disappear or leaves a dead stream waiting forever. Suggested bucket: high if established; could-be-highest: false (the examined consequence is final-screen visibility and attachment liveness, not lost execution or data). Confidence: confirmed source refutation, not execution. Source: service/grid_stream.rs:603-626 performs a final cycle before acting on the liveness it read; Exited leaves the attachment running, Gone reports TerminalEnded, and Unavailable reports StreamFailed. Its wait_for_work at 631-677 follows the runtime status watch and its closure, independently of the removed ticker-driven tmux latch. GridSender::run at 937-965 selects teardown against the whole stream. service/connection.rs:1272-1326 reports natural end/failure via a separate arbiter; detach_naturally at 1486-1519 identity-checks the originating task so a stale end cannot detach its replacement. Contract: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 2898-2905 promises an exited session's terminal remains viewable; SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, runtime paragraph at 2124-2128 says the processed exit follows drained output, while Grid streams at 2650-2656 distinguishes program exit from a gone host. proposed_drop: refuted by the replacement's runtime liveness/watch and final-cycle behavior; the removed latch was for a tmux attachment no longer constructed. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: this is the deletion's interface check; it does not claim an exhaustive review of grid rendering or host journaling.

event.summary: Takeover drops the old input side before constructing the replacement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether replacing AttachBackend with a bare HostAttach and dropping it without joining its pump lets queued keys from the displaced viewer enter after a new viewer takes control. Suggested bucket: high for mixed terminal input if established; could-be-highest: true if such mixed input executed an unintended destructive command, but that route is not established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the replacement-starts-before-cancellation premise; no runtime observation. Source: service/handlers.rs:1729-1969 holds attachments across extraction, signalling, joining and replacement installation. Each old ActiveAttach's remaining fields, including input, are dropped in the doomed loop at 1876-1886; HostAttach::new for the replacement runs only at 1935. HostAttach::drop (grid_stream.rs:1169-1175) sends the cancellation, and Pump::run (1201-1241) checks cancellation first both outside and inside the input handover. It cannot resume unsent old input after that signal; input already handed to the runtime belongs to its ordered queue. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams ends with the exact contract: 'An attachment that ends drops the input its pump had not handed to the runtime and stops the pump at once; what the pump handed over is written before anything a replacement attachment sends.' proposed_drop: refuted by the teardown-before-construction ordering and biased cancellation, rather than specification permission to mix input. possible_cover: none searched. Caveat: this checks the removed backend's ownership handoff, not every producer or connection-loss epoch inside the host runtime.

event.summary: Check whether an input handover already being polled can outlive takeover cancellation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The prior candidate refutation proves the cancellation signal precedes replacement construction, but a pump concurrently inside a poll of its handover may not observe that signal before enqueueing. The exact remaining check is whether InputSequence::send/send_paste has an ordering or ownership fence that prevents such an in-flight old handover from entering behind new-viewer input; biased select alone only prioritizes cancellation when it is polled. Source already checked: handlers.rs:1729-1969 serializes attachment replacement, grid_stream.rs:1169-1175 signals input-pump cancellation without joining, 1201-1262 races cancellation with handover. Suggested bucket: high if mixed input established; could-be-highest: true if mixed terminal commands cause destructive execution, not established. Confidence: unverified lead pending source analysis of InputSequence and the runtime queue. proposed_drop: not settled; prior c4 refutation is narrowed to cancellation-before-construction, not proof of all concurrent handovers. possible_cover: none. No runtime reproduction requested or performed. Next checks: inspect host runtime InputSequence contract, queue admission and whether this behavior existed unchanged before the assigned deletion.

event.summary: Input-pump handover race is a pre-existing interface concern, not created by this removal
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; exclusive review base: 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a. TLDR: An old viewer's pump may already be polling its send when takeover signals cancellation. Without joining that pump, an old send might enter behind the replacement viewer's input, potentially changing a terminal command. Suggested bucket: high for mixed input if established; could-be-highest: true if mixed input executes a destructive command. Confidence: likely concurrency concern with the precise premise that an already-running send poll can enqueue after cancellation while replacement input has become runnable; no execution observed. Investigation: grid_stream.rs:1169-1175 only sends cancellation and never joins the pump; 1201-1241 uses biased selects, which prioritize a cancellation only when polled and do not preempt the handover branch mid-poll. hosts/terminal.rs:1527-1535 and 2320-2339 use an ordinary mpsc send, with a connection epoch rather than an attachment ownership fence. Thus the initial c4 claim that cancellation ordering refuted every concurrent handover was too strong and is retracted; the possible mixed-input consequence is preserved here. Scope checks: git diff from the exclusive base to this commit's parent for service/grid_stream.rs is empty. The assigned commit's diff for that file changes comments and GridSender cleanup notification only; HostAttach, Pump and their cancellation/send behavior are unchanged. At the parent handlers.rs:2047-2069 the old AttachBackend::Host(input) is dropped after the output forwarder joins, without awaiting the pump; at the reviewed revision handlers.rs:1876-1886 drops the same HostAttach after the same output join, before replacement construction at 1935. The removed output-reap barriers track only the output task, never the input pump. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams promises input handed over precedes replacement input, and input not handed over is dropped. proposed_drop: outside the assigned removal and pre-existing before the exclusive range in the unchanged input-pump mechanism; refer to the parent as an interface concern if a broader review is desired. This is a scope proposal, not a source refutation or acceptance by the spec. possible_cover: none searched. Exact remaining uncertainty: no production scheduler interleaving or destructive command has been observed, and no reproduction is authorized. Source comparison settles that the assigned removal adds no new pump synchronization loss; a dedicated source review of the existing pump contract, or an explicitly authorized concurrency test, would judge the broader concern. This resolves the c4 lead for the assigned scope; it does not certify the broader pump behavior safe.

event.summary: Keep unchanged already-polled handover separate from newly delayed natural-detach cancellation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333; exclusive review base: 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a. TLDR and original strongest consequence preserved: queued old-viewer input may enter behind replacement input and change a terminal command, potentially executing destructive input. Suggested bucket: high for an established mixed-input consequence; could-be-highest: true if the mixed command executes a destructive action. Confidence for the original already-polled concern: likely with the precise premise that the old pump is inside a ready send poll when cancellation is signalled and can enqueue after replacement input; no execution or destructive command observed. Original investigation still applies: HostAttach::drop at grid_stream.rs:1169-1175 only signals cancellation; Pump::run:1201-1241 prioritizes it at poll boundaries, not during a poll. InputSequence::send at hosts/terminal.rs:1527-1535 and queue_input:2320-2339 use mpsc admission and a connection epoch, with no attachment ownership fence. The initial broad c4 safety refutation remains retracted. Original proposed_drop basis is preserved as a pending scope proposal only: the HostAttach/Pump mechanism is unchanged from the exclusive base to the reviewed commit's parent (empty diff), and the reviewed diff changes no pump cancellation or input admission code. The removed output reapers never joined the input pump. Parent has accepted no drop or lowering. possible_cover: none searched; caller-supplied g124/l1 is a related, distinct finding rather than coverage of this original concern. Required cross-group synthesis before discovery: g124/l1 establishes a different source lifetime gap, not the original already-polled race. Checked reviewed connection.rs:1510-1517: the natural-detach task moves old.forwarder only, releases attachments at 1515, notifies at 1516, and only then drops the remaining old.input at the block end. The immediate parent connection.rs:2172-2189 explicitly binds and drops backend at 2187 before releasing attachments at 2188. Exclusive-base connection.rs still has this explicit drop at 2187. Therefore an old pump not polled yet can begin before it has received any cancellation, after replacement admission; that particular regression is in-range and is not dismissed by c4's original pre-range comparison. The pinned ActiveAttach replacement at terminals.rs:458 supplies the ordinary HostAttach field whose drop controls that cancellation. Contract remains SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Grid streams: an attachment ending drops input not handed to its runtime, while already handed input precedes replacement input. Restoring drop-before-unlock addresses the new delay, but does not certify against the unchanged mid-poll concern. Caller-supplied trigger evidence retained with priority caveat: g124/l1 traces an accepted authenticated API size of 1001 columns to a live host runtime and grid output encoding failure, then natural detach; the bundled GUI itself clamps size to 1000. This reviewer independently checked the source lifetime ordering above, not every link of that size-producer route. Preserve g124/l1's potential highest command-execution consequence and its explicit accepted-API versus bundled-GUI producer distinction for the parent's priority judgment; neither becomes a source refutation here. No new ID or independent discovery is claimed for this already-known interface finding. The remaining uncertainty for the original c4 concern is the actual production interleaving and harmful mixed-command route, not an uninvestigated missing source fence. Source-only analysis; no tests or reproductions.
